chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ubays ibn Hisham narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Jubla narrated to us, from his father, from Muhammad ibn al-Samit, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him: 'Are there any signs preceding this matter?' He said: 'Yes.' I asked: 'What are they?' He said: 'The perishment of the Abbasid, the rising of al-Sufyani, the killing of the pure soul, the sinking in the Baida', and the call from the heaven.' I said: 'May I be your ransom, I fear that this matter may take a long time?' He said: 'No, it is like the beads of a rosary, one following the other.'

key_terms.أَمْرُ: The Matter, referring specifically to the reappearance (al-Zuhur) of the Imam al-Qa'im.
key_terms.السُّفْيَانِي: Al-Sufyani, a specific figure who rises as a major sign before the reappearance of the Imam.
key_terms.الصَّوْتُ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ: The Call from Heaven, a miraculous audible sign preceding the reappearance.
key_terms.النَّفْسُ الزَّكِيَّةُ: The Pure Soul, a prominent figure martyred before the appearance of the Imam.
key_terms.الْبَيْدَاءُ: Al-Baida, a desert region where a major event (sinking) will occur.

ai.seo_question: What are the five major signs preceding the appearance of the Mahdi according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* identifies five pivotal eschatological markers, with the martyrdom of al-Nafs al-Zakiyya (often identified as Ja'far al-Sadiq or his son) serving as a critical precursor to the Sufyani's uprising. The Imam’s metaphor of beads on a rosary (*nizam al-kharaz*) emphasizes the deterministic and rapid succession of these events, reassuring believers that the period of occultation or waiting will not be drawn out indefinitely. This sequence underscores the Shia theological view of divine timing, where historical upheavals are tightly linked to the ultimate establishment of justice.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (21) Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Sa’eed narrated from al-Qassim bin Muhammad from Obayss bin Hisham from Abdullah bin Jibilla from his father that Muhammad bin as-Samit had said:

“I asked Abu Abdullah as-Sadiq (as): “Will there be certain signs before this matter (the appearance of al-Qa’im)?” He said: “Yes, there will.” I asked: “What are they?” He said: “The perishment of the Abbasids, the rising of al-Sufyani, killing the pure innocent man, the sinking of the desert and the call from the Heaven.” I said: “May I die for you! I am afraid that these things may take a long time!” He said: “No. They will be like the beads of a rosary; one coming after the other.”
